metadata.goal: Analyze how taxi drivers differ in their spatial and operational patterns.
metadata.category: Driver spatial reach, long-distance work, and route-speed stability
metadata.header: Porto Taxi Driver Spatial and Route-Behavior Patterns
metadata.dataset_description: A constructed panel of 648 Porto taxi trips from 18 drivers, with dense OSM-aligned GPS paths, driver-level service footprints, operating hours, trip-distance classes, route directness, and speed variability.
metadata.metric_note: route_directness_ratio is travelled road distance divided by straight-line endpoint distance; higher values indicate more detour, while values nearer 1 indicate a more direct route.

insights: Drivers show distinct spatial routines: some repeatedly serve compact areas, while others operate across a much broader portion of Porto.
Drivers with more long-distance trips cover broader service areas and work later hours than drivers dominated by shorter trips.
Drivers with higher route directness ratios tends to maintain stable speeds, while drivers with lower route directness ratios show more variable in speeds even on long and direct route.
summary: Porto drivers range from compact repeated service routines to broad citywide operation. Higher long-distance shares coincide with wider service coverage and later work. A separate driver grouping shows stable long-trip speeds at higher route-directness ratios and greater speed variation among lower-ratio, more direct routes.
